*Notation.* The problem reuses the symbol $f$ for two different maps. I write $p:Y\to A$ for the map to $A$ from $Y$, and $h:X_1\to X_2$ for the map satisfying $g_2\circ h=g_1$.

**Proof.**

We work in the category of topological spaces equipped with the Quillen (Strom–Serre) model structure: weak equivalences are weak homotopy equivalences, fibrations are Serre fibrations. This model structure is **right proper**: the pullback of a weak homotopy equivalence along a Serre fibration is again a weak homotopy equivalence. (A proof of right properness is included at the end for completeness.)

The argument proceeds in three stages.

---

**Stage 1 — Fibrant replacement of the legs over $A$.**

Factor $g_2:X_2\to A$ as a trivial cofibration followed by a Serre fibration:
$$X_2 \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} E \xrightarrow{\;q\;} A, \qquad q\text{ a Serre fibration.}$$
Factor $g_1:X_1\to A$ similarly:
$$X_1 \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} E_1 \xrightarrow{\;q_1\;} A, \qquad q_1\text{ a Serre fibration.}$$

By the standard characterization of homotopy pullbacks in a right proper model category, the ordinary pullback along a fibrant leg computes the homotopy pullback:
$$Y\times^h_A X_2 \;\simeq\; Y\times_A E, \qquad Y\times^h_A X_1 \;\simeq\; Y\times_A E_1.$$
These weak equivalences are natural with respect to maps of cospans (this is the homotopy invariance of homotopy pullbacks).

---

**Stage 2 — The map $h$ induces a weak equivalence $E_1\xrightarrow{\sim} E$ over $A$.**

Since $g_2\circ h = g_1$, the outer square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
X_1 & \xrightarrow{\;(X_2\to E)\circ h\;} & E \\[4pt]
\downarrow{\sim} & & \downarrow{q} \\[4pt]
E_1 & \xrightarrow{\;q_1\;} & A
\end{array}$$
commutes (the top composite maps to $A$ as $q\circ(X_2\to E)\circ h = g_2\circ h = g_1 = q_1\circ(X_1\to E_1)$). The left vertical map $X_1\to E_1$ is a trivial cofibration; the right vertical map $q$ is a fibration. By the **lifting axiom** of the model structure, there exists a diagonal fill $\phi:E_1\to E$ with
$$q\circ\phi = q_1, \qquad \phi\circ(X_1\to E_1) = (X_2\to E)\circ h.$$

Now apply the **2-out-of-3 property**. The three maps $X_1\to E_1$, $h:X_1\to X_2$, and $X_2\to E$ are all weak equivalences (the first and third by the factorization, the second by hypothesis). Since $\phi\circ(X_1\to E_1)=(X_2\to E)\circ h$, the map $\phi:E_1\to E$ is a weak equivalence as well. Moreover $\phi$ lies **over $A$**: $q\circ\phi=q_1$.

---

**Stage 3 — Pull back and apply right properness.**

The induced map on the representing pullbacks is
$$\Phi: Y\times_A E_1 \longrightarrow Y\times_A E, \qquad (y,e_1)\longmapsto (y,\phi(e_1)),$$
which is well-defined because $q(\phi(e_1))=q_1(e_1)=p(y)$.

Observe that $\Phi$ is the pullback of the weak equivalence $\phi:E_1\xrightarrow{\sim} E$ along the projection
$$\pi_2: Y\times_A E \longrightarrow E, \qquad (y,e)\longmapsto e.$$
The map $\pi_2$ is a **Serre fibration**, being the pullback of the Serre fibration $q:E\to A$ along $p:Y\to A$:
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times_A E & \xrightarrow{\pi_2} & E \\
\downarrow & & \downarrow{q} \\
Y & \xrightarrow{p} & A
\end{array}$$

By **right properness**, pulling back the weak equivalence $\phi$ along the fibration $\pi_2$ yields a weak equivalence:
$$\Phi: Y\times_A E_1 \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} Y\times_A E.$$

---

**Conclusion.**

We have a commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
Y\times^h_A X_1 & \xrightarrow{\;\text{induced}\;} & Y\times^h_A X_2 \\
\downarrow{\sim} & & \downarrow{\sim} \\
Y\times_A E_1 & \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} & Y\times_A E
\end{array}$$
in which the left and right vertical maps are weak equivalences (homotopy invariance of the homotopy pullback, Stage 1) and the bottom map is a weak equivalence (Stage 3). By **2-out-of-3**, the top horizontal map — the induced map $Y\times^h_A X_1\to Y\times^h_A X_2$ — is a weak homotopy equivalence. $\blacksquare$

---

**Appendix: Right properness of spaces.**

For completeness, here is why the Quillen model structure on topological spaces (weak homotopy equivalences, Serre fibrations) is right proper. Given a pullback square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
E' & \xrightarrow{\;\bar f\;} & E \\
\downarrow{p'} & & \downarrow{p} \\
B' & \xrightarrow{\;f\;} & B
\end{array}$$
with $p$ a Serre fibration and $f$ a weak homotopy equivalence, we show $\bar f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Fix $e'\in E'$ with image $e=\bar f(e')\in E$, $b'=p'(e')\in B'$, $b=p(e)=f(b')\in B$. The fiber $F'=p'^{-1}(b')$ identifies with $F=p^{-1}(b)$ (both are $\{(e,b')\in E\times B' : p(e)=f(b')\}$ and $\{e\in E:p(e)=b\}$ respectively, via the pullback). Under this identification the map on fibers $F'\to F$ induced by $\bar f$ is the identity. The Serre fibrations $p'$ and $p$ yield long exact sequences of homotopy groups, and the map $f:B'\to B$ induces isomorphisms $\pi_n(B',b')\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_n(B,b)$ for all $n$ (since $f$ is a weak equivalence). The five lemma applied to the map of long exact sequences gives $\pi_n(E',e')\xrightarrow{\sim}\pi_n(E,e)$ for all $n$ and all basepoints $e'$. Hence $\bar f$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. $\square$
